title: Persistent E2E database path can leak state across runs
reasoning: The E2E settings hard-code a shared SQLite database at /tmp/bahk_e2e.sqlite3. Because the database is intentionally persistent and not namespaced per run, stale rows, schema state, or a partially-written database from a prior failed run can affect later E2E runs. Parallel CI jobs or local runs on the same machine can also contend for the same file, producing nondeterministic failures or false passes.
recommendation: Use a run-specific database name, cleanly recreate the database before each E2E run, or make the persistent path configurable via an environment variable that CI sets uniquely per job.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise application behavior but do not validate E2E database isolation or repeated/parallel execution behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small settings-level test or E2E bootstrap check that confirms the E2E database path is unique to the current run or is reset before tests execute.
minimumFixScope: Update tests/e2e_settings.py and the E2E runner/bootstrap to isolate or reset the SQLite database.
